entries.title: AI Character Sheet Prompts
entries.summary: Create one character and keep them consistent across every image — turnaround sheet, expressions, outfits and scenes. Works for mascots, comic panels and brand avatars.
inside: A master character brief you fill in once
Turnaround sheet prompt (front, side, back, ¾)
Outfit variations without losing the face
Placing the character into any scene
steps: Fill in the master brief with your character's details and save it.
Run the turnaround prompt and pick the best sheet — this becomes your reference image.
For every new image, attach the reference sheet and paste the scene prompt.
If the face drifts, re-attach the sheet and add the line 'match the reference exactly'.

prompts.title: 1 · Master character brief
prompts.text:
You are a character designer. Help me lock a consistent character for an illustration series. Ask me nothing — fill any gaps with sensible choices and list them at the end.

Character: [name], [age], [role/occupation]
Look: [face shape], [skin tone], [hair style + colour], [eye colour], [build]
Signature details: [glasses / scar / earrings / freckles]
Default outfit: [top], [bottom], [shoes], [one accessory]
Personality in 3 words: [word], [word], [word]
Art style: [e.g. clean 2D flat illustration / Pixar-like 3D / anime / realistic photo]

Return a single paragraph 'CHARACTER DNA' under 80 words that I can paste at the start of every future prompt.

prompts.title: 2 · Turnaround sheet
prompts.text:
[paste CHARACTER DNA]

Create a character turnaround reference sheet on a plain off-white background. Show the same character four times in a row, full body, evenly spaced: front view, three-quarter view, side profile, back view. Neutral standing pose, arms relaxed. Identical proportions, face, hair and outfit in every view. Even studio lighting, no shadows on the background, no text, no extra props.

prompts.title: 3 · Expression sheet
prompts.text:
[paste CHARACTER DNA]

Using the attached reference sheet, create an expression sheet: a 4×2 grid of head-and-shoulders portraits of the same character showing happy, laughing, surprised, thinking, confident, worried, angry and calm. Keep the face structure, hairstyle and colours identical to the reference. Plain off-white background, no text labels.

prompts.title: 4 · Outfit variation
prompts.text:
[paste CHARACTER DNA]

Using the attached reference sheet, show the same character in a new outfit: [describe outfit]. Change ONLY the clothing. Face, hair, body proportions and art style must match the reference exactly. Full body, front three-quarter view, plain background.

prompts.title: 5 · Place into a scene
prompts.text:
[paste CHARACTER DNA]

Using the attached reference sheet, place the character in this scene: [location], [time of day], doing [action]. Camera: [close-up / medium / wide], [eye level / low angle]. Mood: [mood]. The character must match the reference exactly — same face, hair, outfit and art style. The background follows the same art style.

entries.title: AI Video Storyboard Prompts
entries.summary: Go from a one-line idea to a short AI video: script, shot list, a still for every shot, then motion prompts for each still. Built for 15–30 second reels.
inside: A checklist for stitching it together
steps: Run the script prompt with your idea and trim it until it reads in 20 seconds.
Turn the script into a shot list and keep it to 5–7 shots.
Generate one still per shot — reuse the same style line in every prompt.
Animate each still with the motion prompt, then cut them together in CapCut or any editor.

prompts.title: 1 · Idea to script
prompts.text:
Write a script for a vertical 20-second video.
Idea: [one line]
Audience: [who]
Goal: [make them follow / visit / DM / buy]

Rules: open with a hook in the first 2 seconds, one idea only, spoken lines under 50 words in total, end with one clear call to action. Return a table: time | what we see | what we hear.

prompts.title: 2 · Script to shot list
prompts.text:
Turn this script into a shot list of 5–7 shots for a 9:16 video.
[paste script]

For each shot give: shot number, duration in seconds, framing (close-up / medium / wide), camera movement (static / slow push-in / pan / handheld), subject and action, and one line of lighting/mood. Also write one STYLE LINE (under 25 words) that describes the look of the whole video.

prompts.title: 3 · Shot to still image
prompts.text:
[STYLE LINE]

Vertical 9:16 frame. [framing] of [subject] [action] in [location]. [lighting/mood]. Clean composition with the subject in the centre third, space at the top for captions. No text, no watermarks.

prompts.title: 4 · Still to motion
prompts.text: Animate this image for [duration] seconds. Camera: [slow push-in / gentle pan left / static]. Subject motion: [one small, natural movement — e.g. turns head toward camera and smiles]. Background: subtle movement only ([steam / leaves / light flicker]). Keep the face and outfit unchanged. Realistic physics, no morphing, no new objects.

entries.title: Product Photo Prompts for Small Brands
entries.summary: Turn one plain phone photo of your product into studio, lifestyle and festive shots for your store and Instagram — without a photoshoot.
inside: Lifestyle scene in a real setting
steps: Take a sharp photo of the product in daylight on a plain surface.
Attach it to the chat and paste one of the prompts below.
Check labels and logos closely — ask for a redo if any text changed.
Export at 4:5 for Instagram feed and 1:1 for your store.

prompts.title: 1 · Studio packshot
prompts.text: Using the attached photo of my product, create a professional studio packshot. Keep the product's shape, colours, label and logo exactly as they are. Place it on a [white / warm beige / soft grey] seamless background with a soft shadow beneath. Soft, even studio lighting from the left. Square 1:1, product centred and filling about 60% of the frame.

prompts.title: 2 · Lifestyle scene
prompts.text: Using the attached photo of my product, place it naturally into this setting: [a sunlit kitchen counter / a café table / a bedside shelf]. Add 2–3 props that suit [my brand vibe], slightly out of focus. Natural window light, warm tones, shallow depth of field. Do not change the product's design, label or colours. Vertical 4:5.

prompts.title: 3 · Festive campaign
prompts.text: Using the attached photo of my product, create a [Diwali / Christmas / Eid / summer sale] campaign image. Product in the foreground, sharp and unchanged. Background themed with [diyas and marigolds / fairy lights / etc.], warm bokeh. Leave clear empty space at the top for a headline. No text in the image. Vertical 4:5.

prompts.title: 4 · Flat-lay
prompts.text: Using the attached photo of my product, create a top-down flat-lay on a [linen / marble / wooden] surface with [3–4 related items] arranged around it. Product in the centre, unchanged. Soft daylight, minimal shadows, calm and tidy composition. Square 1:1.

entries.title: Reel Scripts for Local Businesses
entries.summary: A month of reel ideas, hooks and scripts for a salon, café, clinic, gym or shop — written in your voice, with a comment or DM call to action built in.
inside: Business profile prompt the AI remembers
Full script with on-screen text and caption
steps: Run the business profile prompt first and keep the chat open.
Ask for 30 ideas, then star the 8 you can actually film this month.
Generate hooks for each starred idea and pick the most specific one.
Write the script, film it on your phone and post with the caption it gives you.

prompts.title: 1 · Business profile
prompts.text:
Remember this business for the rest of our chat.
Business: [name], a [type of business] in [area/city]
Customers: [who they are, age, what they care about]
What makes us different: [2–3 points]
Prices: [range]
Tone: [friendly / premium / funny / straight-talking], language: [English / Hinglish / Hindi / Bengali]
Goal for Instagram: [bookings / walk-ins / WhatsApp enquiries]

Reply only with 'Got it' and a one-line summary.

prompts.title: 2 · 30 reel ideas
prompts.text: Give me 30 reel ideas for this business, 6 each in these types: behind the scenes, customer before/after or result, myth vs fact, day-in-the-life, offer or announcement. Each idea in one line, filmable on a phone by one person in under 15 minutes.

prompts.title: 3 · Hook generator
prompts.text: For this reel idea: [idea], write 10 opening hooks under 9 words each. Mix: a bold claim, a question, a number, a mistake people make, and 'POV'. Make them specific to our area and customers, not generic.

prompts.title: 4 · Full script
prompts.text: Write a 20–25 second reel script for: [idea], starting with this hook: [hook]. Give: shot-by-shot what to film, what to say, on-screen text for each shot, and end with this call to action: 'Comment [WORD] and we'll DM you [the offer/price list/booking link]'. Then write a caption under 60 words with 5 local hashtags.

entries.title: How Comment-to-DM Automation Works
entries.summary: The setup behind every 'comment X and I'll send it to you' reel — what Instagram allows, what it costs, and the rules that keep your account safe.
inside: The flow from comment to DM, step by step
What Instagram's API allows (and the 24-hour rule)

blocks.p: Someone comments a keyword on your reel. Instagram sends that comment to your automation through a webhook. The automation checks the keyword, replies publicly to the comment ('Sent! Check your DMs'), and sends a private DM with your link or file. When they tap a button in that DM, the conversation opens and you can keep talking.

Business and creator accounts can reply privately to a comment once, within 7 days of the comment. After the person messages you or taps a button, you have a 24-hour window to send them anything — menus, links, follow-up questions. Every new message from them resets the 24 hours. Outside that window you can't message them, so good automations always end with a reason for the person to reply.

A DM can carry up to 3 buttons. A button either opens a link or sends a hidden reply back to your automation, so you can build menus: 'Get the template', 'See prices', 'Talk to us'. Quick-reply chips (up to 13) and carousels of up to 10 cards are also allowed. That's how a single comment turns into a small conversation — and a lead.

Instagram doesn't charge per message, unlike WhatsApp. You need a Meta developer app, an Instagram professional account and somewhere to run the automation — a self-hosted n8n server costs a few hundred rupees a month, or you can use a tool that does it for you.

Never DM people who didn't comment or message first. Reply to each comment once. Ignore your own messages so the bot doesn't loop. Keep the keyword obvious in the reel so people know what they'll get.

entries.title: WhatsApp Business: What to Automate First
entries.summary: Five automations that save a local business the most time, in the order we set them up for clients — from the free app to the WhatsApp API.
inside: Free app features most owners never switch on
When you actually need the WhatsApp API

blocks.p: Before paying for anything, switch on the WhatsApp Business app's greeting message, away message, quick replies (type /price to send your price list) and catalogue. That alone answers half the questions you get every day.

Move to the WhatsApp API when more than one person answers chats, when you want to send reminders or broadcasts to hundreds of customers, or when you want replies to happen while you sleep. The API needs a Meta business account and a provider or your own setup.

1) An instant menu reply: prices, location, timings, talk to a person. 2) Booking or order confirmation sent automatically. 3) Reminders a day before appointments. 4) A 'how was it?' message after the visit, with your Google review link. 5) Monthly broadcast to past customers with an offer.

Replies inside 24 hours of the customer's message are free. Messages you start (reminders, offers) are charged per message by Meta and vary by type — utility messages like reminders cost much less than marketing ones. Keep broadcasts relevant and infrequent; people who block you hurt your number's quality rating.

entries.title: n8n Workflow: Instagram Comment → DM
entries.summary: Someone comments a keyword on your reel and instantly gets a public reply plus a DM with your link. Multiple keywords, one simple settings box.
inside: Keyword → reply + link table in one CONFIG box
Skips your own comments so it never loops
steps: Download the file, then in n8n open Workflows → Create → ⋯ → Import from File.
Open the CONFIG node: paste your Instagram token and user ID, then edit the keywords and links.
Set a secret word in 'Verify Token OK?', activate, and paste the webhook URL into your Meta app (subscribe to comments).
Comment the keyword from a second account to test.

blocks.p: You need an Instagram professional account connected to a Meta developer app with Instagram API access, and an n8n instance reachable from the internet (n8n Cloud or self-hosted with HTTPS).

entries.title: n8n Workflow: Instagram DM Menu (START)
entries.summary: Turn your Instagram inbox into a menu. People DM START and get buttons for free resources, your website and 'work with us' — which asks what they need and pings you.
inside: Button menu + quick replies, all editable in CONFIG
Lead step that alerts you on Slack or Discord
Ignores normal chats so real conversations aren't interrupted
steps: Download the file, then in n8n open Workflows → Create → ⋯ → Import from File.
Edit CONFIG: token, user ID, trigger words, menu buttons and answers.
Set the verify word, activate, and subscribe your Meta app webhook to messages and messaging_postbacks.
DM START from a second account to test.

inside: WhatsApp list menu with up to 10 options
Instant text answer for each option
steps: Download the file, then in n8n open Workflows → Create → ⋯ → Import from File.
Edit CONFIG: WhatsApp access token, menu rows and the answer for each row.
Set the verify word, activate, and add the webhook URL in Meta app → WhatsApp → Configuration (subscribe to messages).
Send 'hi' to your business number to test.

Works with any site that can POST a webhook

Create a bot with @BotFather, find your chat id, and paste both into CONFIG.
Activate and point your form at the workflow's webhook URL (POST, JSON).
Submit a test enquiry from your site.

entries.title: AI Headshot & Personal Brand Photo Prompts
entries.summary: Professional headshots and personal-brand photos from a few selfies — LinkedIn, website, podcast cover and 'founder at work' shots that still look like you.
inside: Selfie checklist for the best likeness
Fixing likeness when the face drifts
steps: Take 3–5 well-lit selfies facing a window: front, slight left, slight right, no filters.
Attach them and run the headshot prompt first.
Use the fix-likeness prompt if the face doesn't look like you.
Keep one favourite as a reference for every later prompt.

prompts.title: 1 · Corporate headshot
prompts.text: Using the attached photos of me as the only reference for my face, create a professional headshot. Keep my exact facial features, skin tone, face shape, hairline and eye colour — do not beautify or change my age. Outfit: [navy blazer over a white shirt]. Background: soft neutral grey studio backdrop. Lighting: soft key light from the front-left, gentle fill. Framing: head and shoulders, eyes on the upper third, looking at the camera with a relaxed, confident smile. Photorealistic, 85mm lens look, shallow depth of field.

prompts.title: 2 · Personal brand portrait
prompts.text: Using the attached photos as the reference for my face (keep it identical), create a personal brand portrait for my website. I am a [your role]. Setting: [a bright studio with plants / a modern café / my workspace]. Outfit: [describe]. Pose: [arms relaxed, slight lean, turned 30° to camera]. Mood: warm, approachable, premium. Natural window light, warm colour grade, photorealistic.

prompts.title: 3 · Founder at work
prompts.text: Using the attached photos as the reference for my face, show me working: [sketching on a whiteboard / on a laptop at a wooden desk / talking with a client]. Candid documentary style, not posed, caught mid-action. Environment fits a [your industry] business. Soft daylight, slight film grain, 35mm lens look. Keep my face, hair and build exactly as in the reference.

prompts.title: 4 · Podcast / social cover
prompts.text: Using the attached photos as reference, create a square cover photo of me for a [podcast / YouTube channel] about [topic]. Me on the right third, chest-up, expressive [laughing / pointing / thinking] expression. Clean background in [brand colour] with empty space on the left for a title. Bold, crisp lighting. No text in the image.

prompts.title: 5 · Fix the likeness
prompts.text: This doesn't look enough like me. Compare it with the attached reference photos and correct: [eye shape / nose / jawline / hairline / skin tone / age]. Keep the outfit, background and lighting exactly as they are and change only the face to match the reference.

entries.title: Instagram Carousel Prompts
entries.summary: Turn one idea into a 7-slide carousel people save and share — hook slide, value slides, CTA — plus the design brief and caption.
inside: Slide copy that fits on screen
steps: Run the angles prompt and pick the most specific angle.
Generate the outline, then the slide copy.
Paste the design brief into Canva's Magic Design or follow it by hand.
Post with the caption it writes and pin a comment with your keyword.

prompts.title: 1 · 10 carousel angles
prompts.text: I run [business/creator niche] for [audience]. Give me 10 Instagram carousel angles about [topic]. Mix: a step-by-step, a mistakes list, a before/after, a myth-busting post, a checklist, and a 'save this for later' resource. One line each, specific, no generic titles.

prompts.title: 2 · 7-slide outline
prompts.text: Turn this angle into a 7-slide carousel: [angle]. Slide 1 is a hook under 10 words that creates curiosity. Slides 2–6 each give one idea with a short headline and max 25 words of support. Slide 7 is a call to action: comment [KEYWORD] to get [freebie]. Return as a numbered list.

prompts.title: 3 · Slide copy that fits
prompts.text: Rewrite each slide so it fits on a 1080×1350 slide at a readable size: headline max 6 words, body max 20 words, plain language, no hashtags or emojis in the slides. Keep the order. [paste outline]

prompts.title: 4 · Design brief
prompts.text: Write a design brief for this carousel for Canva: colour palette (3 colours with hex codes) that suits [brand vibe], font pairing, layout for the hook slide vs content slides, where to put the slide number and handle, and one visual idea per slide. [paste slides]

prompts.title: 5 · Caption + CTA
prompts.text: Write an Instagram caption for this carousel: first line repeats the hook differently, 3 short lines of context, then the CTA 'Comment [KEYWORD] and I'll DM you [freebie]'. Under 80 words, 5 niche hashtags at the end. [paste slides]

entries.title: AI Customer Reply Prompts for Small Businesses
entries.summary: Answer DMs, Google reviews, complaints and price questions in your own tone in seconds — polite, on-brand and ready to paste.
inside: Reply to a DM or WhatsApp enquiry
Reply to Google reviews (good and bad)
Handle a complaint without losing the customer
Answer 'how much?' without scaring people off
steps: Run the tone profile first and keep that chat for replies.
Paste the customer's message into the matching prompt.
Read it once, change any detail that isn't true, and send.

prompts.title: 1 · Tone profile
prompts.text: Remember how my business talks for the rest of this chat. Business: [name, what you sell, where]. Tone: [warm and friendly / premium and calm / fun and casual]. Language: [English / Hinglish / Bengali]. We always: [offer to call / share a booking link / sign off with our name]. We never: [promise discounts in chat / use slang]. Reply 'Ready'.

prompts.title: 2 · DM / WhatsApp enquiry
prompts.text: Write a reply to this customer message in our tone. Answer their question directly in the first line, add one helpful detail, and end with a clear next step ([book here / share your date / call us]). Max 60 words. Customer: "[paste message]"

prompts.title: 3 · Google review reply
prompts.text: Write a reply to this Google review. If positive: thank them by name, mention one specific thing they liked, invite them back — max 40 words. If negative: thank them, apologise for the specific issue without excuses, say what we're changing, and offer to fix it offline at [phone/email] — max 70 words. Review: "[paste review]"

prompts.title: 4 · Complaint, calmly
prompts.text: A customer is upset: "[paste message]". Write a reply that acknowledges their feeling in one line, takes responsibility for what went wrong, offers a concrete fix ([refund / redo / discount on next visit]), and moves the chat to a call if needed. No defensive language. Max 80 words.

prompts.title: 5 · 'How much?' answer
prompts.text: A customer asks the price of [service/product]. Our price is [price or range]. Write a reply that gives the price clearly, explains in one line what's included and why it's worth it, and offers a smaller option or a quick call if budget is a concern. Max 60 words, friendly, no pressure.

entries.title: AI Logo & Brand Moodboard Prompts
entries.summary: Explore a brand look before paying a designer — name ideas, moodboards, logo concepts and a one-page brand sheet you can hand over.
steps: Answer the brand brief prompt honestly — it shapes everything else.
Generate a moodboard and save the 2–3 directions you like.
Run logo concepts in Ideogram or Midjourney for clean text.
Use the brand sheet prompt to summarise it for a designer.

prompts.title: 1 · Brand brief
prompts.text: Interview me to build a brand brief. Ask me 8 short questions one at a time about: what I sell, who it's for, what makes it different, 3 words the brand should feel like, brands I admire, colours I love and hate, where it will be seen most, and the price level. After my last answer, summarise the brief in 8 bullet points.

prompts.title: 2 · Names and taglines
prompts.text: Using this brief, suggest 15 brand names in 3 styles (descriptive, invented, metaphor) and check each is short, easy to spell and say. Then write 5 taglines under 6 words for my favourite: [name]. [paste brief]

prompts.title: 3 · Moodboard
prompts.text: Create a brand moodboard grid for [brand name], a [what it is] for [audience]. Brand feeling: [3 words]. Include: a colour palette swatch strip, a typography sample, 2 product/lifestyle photos, a texture, and a pattern. Cohesive, editorial layout on an off-white background. Style: [minimal / bold / earthy / luxurious].

prompts.title: 4 · Logo concepts
prompts.text: Logo design for "[brand name]": a [wordmark / icon + wordmark / monogram]. Style: [flat, geometric, minimal]. Colours: [hex codes]. The icon suggests [idea, e.g. a leaf forming a cup]. Clean vector look, centred on a plain white background, no mockups, no extra text, high contrast. Show 4 variations in a 2×2 grid.

prompts.title: 5 · One-page brand sheet
prompts.text: Turn everything we decided into a one-page brand sheet for a designer: name, tagline, audience, personality (3 words + what it's not), colour palette with hex codes and usage %, fonts (heading/body with Google Fonts alternatives), logo direction, photo style, and 5 do's and don'ts.

entries.title: AI Weekly Planning & Focus Prompts
entries.summary: A calm Sunday planning routine with AI — brain dump to prioritised week, time-blocked days and a Friday review. Pairs well with Notion.
inside: Friday review that improves next week
steps: Every Sunday, dump everything on your mind into the first prompt.
Let it sort and choose your top 3 — then you decide.
Copy the time-blocked plan into your calendar or Notion.
Run the Friday review and save the lessons.

prompts.title: 1 · Brain dump sorter
prompts.text: Here is everything on my mind this week, unsorted: [paste brain dump]. Sort it into: Must do this week, Should do, Could do, Delegate, Delete. Flag anything with a deadline. Estimate time for each must-do in 15-minute blocks. Return as a checklist.

prompts.title: 2 · Top 3 for the week
prompts.text: My goals this quarter are: [goals]. From my must-do list, choose the 3 tasks that move those goals forward most and explain why in one line each. Then tell me which task I'm probably avoiding and the smallest first step to start it.

prompts.title: 3 · Time-block my days
prompts.text: Plan my week in time blocks. My working hours are [hours], I have these fixed commitments: [meetings/classes]. I focus best in the [morning/afternoon]. Put deep work for the top 3 in my best hours, batch small tasks together, leave 20% of the time free for surprises. Return a day-by-day table.

prompts.title: 4 · Daily check-in
prompts.text: Quick daily check-in. Yesterday I planned: [plan]. I actually did: [what happened]. Today's fixed commitments: [list]. Give me today's plan in 5 lines max, starting with the one task that matters most.

prompts.title: 5 · Friday review
prompts.text: Run a weekly review with me. What I planned: [top 3 + plan]. What happened: [notes]. Ask me 3 sharp questions about what worked and what didn't, then give me 2 changes to try next week and 1 thing to stop doing.
